# leafwiki: widespread quiet misbehaviour, diagnosed without a test suite

A self-hosted server for a hierarchy of written documents, each with its own files, history and full-text lookup, is now quietly wrong across a wide spread of everyday operations. Nothing about the protocol, the stored data or the callers changed. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that has been observed from the outside, described by what someone was doing at the time.

Someone tidying up a document and the files hanging off it runs into trouble at almost every step. A file uploaded to a document still answers 201 and its bytes land on disk, but asking the server for that document's files comes back as a failure rather than the expected single-entry listing. Renaming one of those files through the API answers with an error status too, while uploading and deleting a single file still return 2xx and still write a history entry crediting the signed-in account. Asking for every file of a document to be removed reports success and removes nothing — a listing afterwards still shows the file that was uploaded. Duplicating a document that has one image hanging off it creates the copy, but the copy ends up with no files at all. Reordering the children of an ordinary parent no longer takes effect: submitting an explicit order for two children either fails outright or leaves them in their original order when reloaded.
